results.title: Food, Beverage, and Consumer Products Issues to Watch for 2026
results.content: In addition to updated guidance, entities subject to the FDA’s human food regulations should expect continued efforts to improve alignment between inspections and enforcement activities through the HFP’s Office of Compliance & Enforcement. **In 2026, companies should expect FDA reviewers and inspectors to focus less on technical compliance with former SOI specifications and more on whether product names, statements of identity, and descriptive claims accurately convey the product’s composition and character to consumers.** This means that while revocation of these SOIs allows for greater formulation and innovation flexibility, it also places an increased burden on manufacturers to ensure that labeling accurately reflects the product’s composition. For food, beverage, supplement, and consumer-product companies, 2026 compliance risks include ensuring origin claims are supported by component-level substantiation and avoiding inconsistency between FTC-facing marketing claims and FDA- or USDA-regulated origin statements such as “Made in USA with imported ingredients,” “Packed in USA,” or “Product of USA.”.
